models.model_label: Conditional logit of the going-private decision, full matched sample
models.sample_description: Full pre- and post-SOX matched case-control sample: 237 going-private firms and 237 non-going-private controls (N=474). Each control is matched to a going-private firm using prior-year market value and SIC industry; when a four-digit SIC match is unavailable, the authors use three- or two-digit SIC. The market-value caliper is |ln(firm market value) - ln(control firm market value)| < ln(4), using natural logarithms. Filings run from January 1998 through May 2005; the sample includes both pre- and post-SOX proposal-announcement periods.
models.method_details: The authors explicitly report conditional-logit regressions for the binary going-private decision in the matched case-control sample.

dependent_variable.name: GoingPrivate_i
dependent_variable.definition: Indicator equal to 1 for going-private firms and 0 for matched control firms.
dependent_variable.formula: 1 for a going-private firm; 0 for a control firm.

evidence.quote: Dependent variable 1⁄4 1 for going-private firms, 0 for control firms.

scope.quote: In this paper, we provide evidence on the effect of SOX on firms that are close to the public/private margin; that is, firms for which the net benefits of being public are relatively small. Specifically, we examine firms’ going-private decisions, and ask how this choice was affected by SOX.

We pose three main questions regarding SOX and the going-private decision. First, to what extent was SOX associated with an increase in the number of firms electing to go private? Second, did the factors associated with firms’ decisions to go private change around the passage of SOX? Third, did the determinants of going-private announcement returns change around the passage of SOX?
Given our interest in how SOX has changed the public/private margin, we examine whether the characteristics related to the likelihood of firms going private differ in the pre- and post-SOX periods.
In Table 8, we present the results of the logit regressions. Column (1) includes all firms, Column (2) includes pre-SOX firms only, and Columns (3)–(5) include post-SOX firms only.

method.quote: Given that going-private firms appear with greater probability in our matched sample than in the population of firms as whole, which biases the parameter estimates in a traditional logit regression (Palepu, 1986), we conduct conditional logit regressions
